profile.title: DFARS 252.204-7012 safeguarding with -7019/-7020 assessment and SPRS scoring
profile.description: NIST SP 800-171 applied to covered defense information under DFARS, with a self-assessment scored on the DoD methodology (110 less weighted deductions) and posted to SPRS. Unlike CMMC Level 1, a POA&M is permitted, which is the sharpest difference between two regimes that read the same control catalog.

citations.title: Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting
citations.note: The clause requiring NIST SP 800-171 implementation for covered defense information, plus incident reporting. The full-implementation date for 800-171 was 2017-12-31.

citations.title: Notice of NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment Requirements
citations.note: Requires a current (within three years) assessment posted in SPRS as a condition of award consideration.

citations.title: NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment Requirements
citations.note: Establishes the Basic/Medium/High assessment levels and the obligation to provide access for higher-level assessments. The self-assessment automat can contribute to is the Basic level.

citations.title: Contractor Compliance with the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Level Requirement
citations.note: CMMC Phase 2 begins 2026-11-10, at which point most CUI contracts require a C3PAO-assessed Level 2 rather than a self-assessment. This profile's `phased` status is that date: the self-assessment path it models is being layered over, not withdrawn, and an operator planning past late 2026 needs to know which regime their next award falls under. Recorded as a citation rather than a separate profile because a Level 2 profile would need C3PAO assessment modeling automat has no basis for yet.

citations.title: Class Deviation — NIST SP 800-171 Revision 2 for DFARS 252.204-7012
citations.note: Pins Revision 2 for DFARS purposes notwithstanding 800-171's own revision to Rev 3. This is why control_catalogs pins r2 rather than leaving the revision to the operator — the instrument answers the question that NIH's notices leave open.

control_catalogs.note: Pinned by the class deviation above, not by automat's preference. The 800-171r2 catalog is not yet built (ROADMAP Phase 0 deferred it; docs/open-questions.md Q4 records the CPRT acquisition path), so artifact_id names the catalog this profile expects rather than one that exists today.

signed_by: The contractor's authorized representative posting the score
A senior official where the institution's own policy requires one
assessment.cadence: at least every three years, and on material change
assessment.notes: The Basic assessment is a self-assessment; Medium and High are performed by the government (DFARS 252.204-7020), and this profile models only the Basic level. The System Security Plan and POA&M are retained and produced on request rather than submitted with the score.

poam.notes: Deducted requirements may carry a plan of action with a target completion date, which is posted alongside the score. Note the interaction with partial_credit: an individual requirement is still binary — SATISFIED or not — and the aggregate score is where degrees are expressed. A POA&M defers the remedy, it does not soften the determination.

weight_table.title: NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment Methodology — per-requirement value table
weight_table.note: NOT YET VENDORED. Q10 is decided (dual independent transcription, hashed, named by the report) but the transcription itself is a Phase 4 deliverable and has not been performed. This entry is present so the profile's shape is reviewable; the hash is 64 zeros, and a test asserts no profile with an unresolved weight-table hash can be used for scoring. Deliberately NOT filled with plausible weights: a wrong weight is confidently wrong in the same direction on every regeneration, and no test catches a false input to correct arithmetic.

submission.notes: SPRS has no documented ingest format; scores are entered through its web application. automat emits the score plus per-requirement worked arithmetic so the operator can key it in and defend it, and formats nothing for submission.

applicability.trigger: A DoD contract or subcontract containing DFARS 252.204-7012, where covered defense information is processed, stored, or transmitted on a contractor information system. For universities the usual path is a subaward or a prime award with the clause flowed down; fundamental research awards frequently do not carry it. Read the award terms and ask your sponsored programs and contracts offices. automat does not and cannot determine this.
hints: The award or subaward includes DFARS 252.204-7012
The award identifies covered defense information or CUI to be handled
SPRS already holds a score for the institution's CAGE code hierarchy
exclusions: Acquisitions solely for commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) items

policy_caveat: automat encodes a technical reading of published policy. It is not legal advice and not a compliance determination. The agreement, award terms, or contract clause your institution signed governs; your sponsored programs office, contracts office, or counsel decides what applies and which revision. Where policy is ambiguous — for example the NIH 800-171 revision question — automat records the operator's declaration rather than resolving it. Policy citations carry effective dates and change; verify against the primary source before relying on them.
